cards.text: POWER: Power is in the hands of community members, thereby, increasing individuals' investment in health and their community and decreasing the power of corporations and big institutions.
FUNDING and BUDGET: Key local public health services are protected and funding for prevention has been assured in perpetuity, lessening the scarcity mindset and changing what we make decisions about.
DECISION MAKING/PLANNING: Funding is stable, so agencies invest in long term plans, but experience has more influence than evidence and inequities exist as planning leaves out those not engaged.
COMPETITION: The broad nature of public health means that housing, transportation, food, caregiving, etc. compete for the same prevention resources.
CROSS-SECTOR WORK/SDOH: In this future public health is intentionally broad and integrated across sectors (e.g. transportation, housing) to access structural levers that impact health.
DECENTRALIZATION: Public health is hyperlocal, posing limits to coordination and state and national strategizing.
